key_insight: Imbibition in realistic cement pores is governed by evolving interface geometry and connectivity, with trapped air slowing saturation even under perfectly water-wetting conditions.
engineering_relevance: Resolving pore-scale water invasion can inform moisture-transport assessment and corrosion-relevant analysis at steel–concrete interfaces.
method: Pore-resolved, multiphase DNS in a 3D FIB–SEM-reconstructed cementitious microstructure.
Resolve transient air–water interfaces from nanometre-to-micrometre spatial scales.
Use controlled 2D analyses to examine scale-dependent force balances.
evidence_signal: The 3D simulations reveal heterogeneous wetting fronts and progressive air entrapment, while comparison with 2D analyses highlights out-of-plane curvature and network connectivity.
watch_item: The abstract reports no direct experimental validation of the resolved transient interfaces, which remain experimentally inaccessible at these scales.
paper_title: Pore-scale mechanisms of capillary imbibition in cement-based materials revealed by direct numerical simulations in a realistic FIB-SEM microstructure
